requirements.requirement: A dedicated inventorysvc account exists on node1.
requirements.summary: The account and matching group exist as system identities; the account has no usable login shell and uses /nonexistent as its home directory.

requirements.requirement: The managed service inventory-worker runs /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker under inventorysvc on node1.
requirements.summary: The systemd unit is named inventory-worker, is enabled and active, specifies the requested executable and inventorysvc user/group, and its observed process runs with UID 999 and GID 988. It also recovered successfully after a genuine node restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Provider-wide restart evidence is complete for node1: it captures a healthy pre-restart service and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered enabled/active service state with no failed units. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot change.
limitations: The first executor command ended with a backend exception, so its complete output is unavailable; the following command nevertheless directly observed the unintended root-run worker process it had started.
No application data or cluster state existed in the public contract to validate after restart; recovery evidence therefore covers the applicable node and service state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene is strong: no failed units, damaged package state, unexpected listening service, or abandoned temporary file is shown. One unnecessary bounded mutation occurred: the discovery command directly launched the worker as root with an unsupported --help argument, leaving a temporary process (cmd-e88efb0708f942dd). The executor then attempted explicit cleanup (cmd-1ad3e6d9036c4c25), and the later restart plus the final process inventory confirm that only the intended inventorysvc-managed instance remained. All other state-changing commands had clear roles in account creation, service installation, activation, required restart evidence, or cleanup.
